picked.title: Triage Before Fine-Tuning: Feasibility-Gated Selection and Monitored Adaptation of Embodied Foundation Models for a Fixed Physical Platform
picked.summary: Embodied foundation models are increasingly deployed by selection: a practitioner picks a public checkpoint by benchmark rank and fine-tunes it on local data. The platform is fixed before the model is chosen, with little or no local data. We ask what such a checkpoint loses on a fixed platform and which part of the loss local data can buy back. We split the gap by what can repair it. A sensing gap, information the sensors do not capture, cannot be closed with their data; a latency gap, output arriving after the control loop needs it, belongs to the loop, not the weights; only a distribution gap is fine-tuning's to repair. TRIAGE turns this into feasibility-gated selection and monitored adaptation in five stages: gates on the sensor contract and on end-to-end latency that no score can override, probes on ten minutes of local logs, a ranking by target-relevant score among the candidates that pass, and fine-tuning that is monitored and checked in closed loop before release. On driving benchmarks, a deadline below a leading closed-loop model's latency makes it collide on 80 to 90% of routes, and losing field of view moves plans 2.2 to 5.7 times more than losing resolution at equal pixels. Local frames close 75% of a stability gap but raise perturbation sensitivity at small budgets, and picking by score violates a gate in two of four deployment profiles. On a full-scale vehicle, the factory camera failed the sensing gate and an added camera repaired it. The latency gate removed the two highest-scoring candidates, neither of which completed a closed-loop trip. The selected model passed acceptance in 4 of 5 closed-loop trips, and the closed-loop check withheld a fine-tuned model that had improved offline. TRIAGE lets organizations that cannot train foundation models from scratch find out whether a public checkpoint can run on the robot or vehicle they own, and what to fix if not.

picked.title: FreshVLA: Frequency-Regularized Time Scale Hierarchical Latent Actions for Vision-Language-Action Models
picked.summary: Learning reusable latent actions from action-free videos offers an effective route to improving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. However, reconstruction-oriented latent actions do not necessarily benefit policy learning: as they may encode task-irrelevant static appearance with scene identity, or entangle slowly varying task progress with fine-grained execution dynamics in limited discrete code. We propose FreshVLA, a VLA framework built on a frequency-guided, dynamics-sensitive learning paradigm for acquiring temporally hierarchical continuous latent actions. FreshVLA uses a high-pass prior to guide visual transition encoding toward dynamical regions, thereby reducing reliance on static appearance cues. It further organizes latent actions into coarse-grained task progress and fine-grained execution dynamics through cross-timescale sampling and frequency-domain regularization, enhancing their capacity to represent long-horizon behaviors. During policy training, we freeze the pretrained latent action encoder and transfer its representations to robot control through joint flow-matching of latent and robot actions. FreshVLA achieves 98.2% average success on LIBERO and 98.0% on LIBERO-Long, exceeding GR00T-N1.6 on the latter by 3.6%. It also reaches an average sequence length of 4.52 on CALVIN and strong overall success rate of 80.4% in the zero-shot LIBERO-PLUS evaluation. Furthermore, FreshVLA exhibits greater robustness to visual perturbations and a more distinct division of roles between two branches in modeling low- and high-frequency motion, respectively. In 35-step action regression, it achieves a 51.3-percentage-point higher relative error reduction than its hierarchical discrete counterpart. Real-world experiments demonstrate that FreshVLA improves the average success rate over $π_{0.5}$ by 7.5%. The FreshVLA project page is available at https://freshvla.github.io/.

picked.title: CamAct: Learning Robotic Manipulation from In-the-Wild Videos via Camera Motion
picked.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models benefit from large, diverse datasets for robotic manipulation, yet collecting robot demonstrations remains costly. Recent work has explored egocentric videos as a source of supervision, primarily drawing on demonstrations of human-object interaction. We show that in-the-wild videos can improve robotic manipulation even when they contain no demonstrations of object manipulation. Specifically, camera motion recovered from these videos provides an additional source of motion supervision that complements robot demonstrations. Building on this finding, we introduce CamAct, which incorporates this camera-motion supervision into VLA policies alongside robot demonstrations, extending the use of human videos for manipulation learning beyond object interactions. Experiments show that incorporating this video supervision during fine-tuning improves success rates from 96.40% to 98.10% on LIBERO and from 22.96% to 29.32% on RoboCasa 365. The resulting policy also demonstrates strong results in out-of-distribution generalization on LIBERO-Plus and real-world manipulation tasks.

picked.title: $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM: Efficient Hierarchical Memory Across Modalities and Timescales for World-Action Models
picked.summary: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires historical context, yet retaining extensive visual histories incurs growing storage and retrieval costs, while aggressive compression risks losing fine-grained information needed for subsequent decisions. Moreover, executed action histories capture intermediate behaviors that sparse visual observations may miss. Preserving this complementary context efficiently calls for modality-specific memory mechanisms that balance recent detail with long-term retention. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM, a world-action model equipped with hierarchical visual and interaction memories. $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM preserves recent visual observations in dense short-term memory while consolidating entries evicted from this window into fixed-size associative long-term memory through gated delta updates. Within the same short- and long-term hierarchy, interaction memory encodes executed action prefixes into compact temporal representations, complementing visual observations with behavioral context. These complementary memories are integrated into world-action modeling through layer-wise retrieval, enabling memory-augmented action generation with a bounded online memory footprint independent of episode length. On the memory-dependent simulation benchmarks MIKASA-Robo and RMBench, $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves +53.2% and +61.2% absolute improvements in average success rates over Fast-WAM, respectively. These gains extend to real-world manipulation, where $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves a +29.3% absolute improvement over LingBot-VA in average success across three tasks. These results suggest that $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM offers a promising approach to efficient memory-augmented world-action modeling.

picked.title: 深耕核心零部件，钛虎机器人轻量化关节模组Lite-1系列助力整机降本增效
picked.summary: 近日，钛虎机器人科技（上海）有限公司（以下简称“钛虎机器人”）正式发布面向机器人批量落地场景的轻量化关节模组Lite-1系列。该产品通过结构精简，驱控板与编码器一体化设计，在压缩体积、提升集成度的同时保持控制精度与运行稳定性，为人形机器人整机设计与规模化生产提供了新的核心零部件选择。 当前，人形机器人产业正从“能走能动”的样机验证阶段，加速迈向“可批量、可交付、可落地”的产业化阶段。关节模组是机器人的核心运动部件，其体积、集成度、走线方式与装配一致性，直接影响整机结构、成本与量产节奏。头部、手臂、腰部等部位空间有限，对关节的轴向尺寸提出了更高要求；多关节带来的复杂线束，也增加了走线与装配难度。关节模组的轻量化并非“减配”，而是通过结构设计优化与集成度提升，在更小的体积内实现同等的控制精度与可靠性。 结构设计：轴向长度较上代至多缩短22.5% 据介绍，该系列采用驱控板与编码器一体化集成，整机部件精简至6个，内部排布更紧凑。同外径尺寸下，关节轴向长度较上代产品至多缩短22.5%；侧出线设计减少线束转弯，使带线轴向安装空间节省多达30%，为人形机器人头部、手腕等部位留出更大设计余量，助力整机外形更贴近人形比例。 驱感一体：兼顾控制精度与运行稳定 集成带来的收益不止于结构层：信号走线更短、链路干扰更低，可支撑整机高频控制与快速响应。关节输出线性度高，搭配双编码器架构，位置反馈更稳定，实现全场景0跳变，运动更平稳精细；低温升特性减少长时间连续运行中的热衰减，为高负载工况下的可靠性与持久性提供支撑。 …

picked.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning
picked.summary: Robot policies deployed in the wild should have the capability to continually learn new tasks without forgetting existing behaviors. A common approach to combat such catastrophic forgetting is to train on new task data with a replay buffer of previously learned task data. Although this buffer is commonly sampled randomly from all prior experiences, we show that a small set of these experiences contributes greatly in anchoring past performance. We call these experiences Memory Anchors. We identify Memory Anchors in regions where representations of new-task observations collapse onto those of old-task observations even though the tasks require conflicting actions, like when a familiar object must be manipulated in a new way. Rehearsing old data in this region plays a key role in preventing destructive overwriting of past task knowledge, serving as this critical Memory Anchor role. Excluding only 10% Memory Anchors before sampling the buffer leads to more than a 4.5x increase in catastrophic forgetting on the LIBERO benchmark suites. Conversely, enriching the replay buffer with Memory Anchors can decrease high-conflict task forgetting by 63% and enables successful continual learning of two task sequences on a real robot. picked.title: 机器人量产背后，物理AI开始算新账：研发底座何必各自建？
picked.summary: 2026年，人形机器人加速走出实验室。 但是让机器人在真实世界产生价值，依然复杂而成本高昂。 从数据采集、物理仿真到模型训练、真机验证，机器人每掌握一项新技能，背后都可能是一整套研发流程的反复运转。 更复杂的是，这些能力分散在不同的专业厂商手中。产业分工越来越细，如何将分散的技术能力组织起来，反而成了一道新的难题。 当机器人开始规模化交付，产业需要解决的不只是如何造出更多机器人，还有如何让更多企业以更低的成本训练机器人。 这也让物理AI产业出现了一个新的机会：谁有能力将分散的研发资源组织成可复用的基础设施，谁就有机会成为产业链上的重要组织者。 九章云极正尝试从算力供应商向物理AI开发平台延伸，通过物理AI工厂、生态联盟和标准化接口，参与这场产业分工的重构。 01 机器人越造越多，研发底座开始走向共建 《2026年人形机器人产业发展报告》显示，今年上半年，中国人形机器人出货量已超过4万台。 机器人走出实验室后，需要掌握更多技能，适应不同的工作环境。每进入一个新的应用场景，机器人企业都可能需要开发新的技能，研发任务也随之增加。 这背后是一条需要不断重复的研发链。 举个简单的例子，智能机器人完成一个抓取动作，要经过数据采集、仿真、训练和真机验证。物理AI的特殊之处就在于，仿真中成功的抓取，可能会因为现实中的光照、物体材质或位置变化而失败。 一旦抓取失败，相关数据还得回流训练，推动下一轮调整。这样的试错可能反复发生，那随之而来的是持续增长的数据处理、仿真和训练需求。 …
